test_title: PYST 58: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements about Presbyopia is correct?

options.text: It is corrected only by concave lenses.
It usually occurs in young children.
It occurs due to weakening of ciliary muscles and loss of lens flexibility.
The near point becomes less than 25 cm.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It occurs due to weakening of ciliary muscles and loss of lens flexibility**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Presbyopia** is a common vision condition that occurs with **aging**, where the eye gradually loses its ability to focus clearly on nearby objects.
 
• It is primarily caused by the **gradual weakening** of the **ciliary muscles** and the diminishing **flexibility** (elasticity) of the **crystalline lens**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The power of **accommodation** of the eye usually decreases with **age**. For most people, the **near point** gradually recedes and becomes **greater than 25 cm**, making it difficult to read comfortably without corrective glasses. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Unlike conditions like Myopia, **Presbyopia** is not typically found in **young children**; it usually becomes noticeable in individuals in their **early to mid-40s** and continues to worsen until around age **65**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• This condition is generally corrected using **convex lenses** (for reading) or **bifocal lenses** if the person also suffers from Myopia. **Concave lenses** are used to correct Myopia (nearsightedness), not Presbyopia alone. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Myopia (Nearsightedness):**
 
 
• In this defect, a person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly.
 
• It occurs due to **excessive curvature** of the eye lens or **elongation** of the eyeball.
 
• It is corrected using a **concave lens** of suitable power.
 
 
 
• **Hypermetropia (Farsightedness):**
 
 
• A person with hypermetropia can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly.
 
• The **near point** for the person is farther away from the normal near point (**25 cm**).
 
• It arises because the **focal length** of the eye lens is too long or the eyeball has become too small.
 
• It is corrected by using a **convex lens** of appropriate power.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism:**
 
 
• This defect arises when the **cornea** is not spherical in shape, leading to different **curvatures** in different planes.
 
• It results in objects appearing blurred or distorted at all distances.
 
• It is typically corrected using **cylindrical lenses**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Power of Accommodation:** The ability of the eye lens to adjust its **focal length** is called accommodation. When muscles are relaxed, the lens is thin and its focal length increases (for distant objects). When **ciliary muscles** contract, the lens becomes thick, and the focal length decreases (for nearby objects).
 
• **Bifocal Lenses:** Sometimes a person suffers from both **Myopia** and **Hypermetropia/Presbyopia**. Such people require **bifocal lenses**. A common type of bifocal lens consists of both concave and convex lenses. The **upper portion** is a **concave lens** (facilitates distant vision), and the **lower part** is a **convex lens** (facilitates near vision).
 
• **Modern Solutions:** Nowadays, vision defects can also be corrected with **contact lenses** or through **surgical interventions** such as **LASIK** (Laser-Assisted In Situ Keratomileusis).
 
• The **least distance of distinct vision** for a normal young adult eye is **25 cm**, and the **far point** is **infinity**.
</ul
